latestVersion.changelog:
Initial release of Data Rights Guard skill.

- Provides a practical framework and workflow for copyright and licensing checks on training data before it enters datasets.
- Helps verify commercial use permissions, license presence, attribution, and source traceability for any data used in AI training, fine-tuning, or evaluation.
- Offers actionable recommendations when trigger keywords or scenarios are detected, preventing unlicensed or non-commercial data from entering training pipelines.
- Delivers deterministic output and clear exit codes (`rc=0` success, `rc=1` issues detected, `rc=2` usage/environment error).
- Designed for local execution with privacy in mind—no data sent to third parties, credentials handled securely.
- Meant as an auxiliary compliance tool, not a replacement for professional or legal judgment.

items.summary: Review a PR, reconcile prior feedback, and watch for the author's fix
items.description: Review a GitHub pull request from a PR number, repo-qualified reference, or URL; reconcile the current content against all earlier review comments so fixes do not regress; post one consolidated PR comment; and watch for the PR author's "addressed" responses until a clean review, at no/low token cost while nothing changes. Use when the user asks to review, babysit, re-check, or continuously monitor a PR until no blocking issues remain, with bounded convergence across follow-up cycles.

items.summary: Build, validate, and open a review-ready PR

Use when starting any change that will become a PR — not just when asked to "open a PR". Never merges and never deploys.
